# Team Health

`customer_support.support_management.team_health` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Can this team keep doing this, and what in the queue is telling us it cannot?**


> Reading whether the people can keep doing this. Support is the only function whose daily work is absorbing other people's frustration, attrition is its dominant cost driver, and burnout is legible in queue data weeks before it is legible in a resignation — quality drifting down while throughput holds, macro use climbing, the same agent taking every escalation because they are the one who can. This is a capability rather than an HR concern precisely because an expert reads it from the tickets, and by the time it reaches a one-to-one the recoverable window has usually closed.

> Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes, playbooks, heuristics, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following quality-assurance in this subdomain. The expertise worth encoding is the set of leading indicators that live in queue data rather than in a survey: unequal distribution of hard work, quality falling while volume holds, rising reliance on canned responses, one person absorbing every out-of-hours page, and the disappearance of the small unpaid acts — updating an article, correcting a macro — that people stop doing first when they are depleted. Also worth stating: an engagement survey measures what people are willing to say about a team they are still in, which is the last place a problem shows up rather than the first.
